description: The bar chart illustrates the comparative performance of two multilingual language models, mBERT and XLM-R, across various language families and isolates, as measured by the number of tasks where one model outperforms the other or they perform equally. The horizontal axis categorizes languages into groups: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, with an unlabeled gray bar between IE-Romance and IE-other that does not correspond to any legend entry and appears to be a visual artifact. The vertical axis, labeled “task count,” ranges from 0 to 40 in increments of 10, representing the number of probing tasks. Three bar types are shown per category: light blue for “mBERT better,” dark blue for “XLM-R better,” and light green for “same,” as indicated in the legend in the upper right. In IE-Baltic, XLM-R better (dark blue) reaches approximately 10 tasks, while same (light green) is around 7; mBERT better is absent. In IE-Germanic, mBERT better is ~4, XLM-R better ~18, and same ~22. In IE-Indic, mBERT better is ~1, XLM-R better ~5, and same ~4. In IE-Romance, mBERT better is ~4, XLM-R better ~13, and same ~30. In IE-other, mBERT better is ~1, XLM-R better ~6, and same ~8. In Isolate, mBERT better is ~1, XLM-R better ~5, and same ~1. In Semitic, mBERT better is ~1, XLM-R better ~7, and same ~1. In Uralic, mBERT better is ~1, XLM-R better ~14, and same ~5. The bars are not sorted by height, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding. The chart visually suggests that XLM-R generally outperforms mBERT across most language families, with IE-Romance showing the highest total task count (mBERT: ~4, XLM-R: ~13, same: ~30), and the “same” category often being the largest bar in many groups.
